Route 1: Chemical Reduction with Hydrazine Hydrate

1. Prepare the copper precursor solution by dissolving Cu(NO₃)₂·2.5H₂O (34.5 mg, concentration 43.0 mM) in deionized water (20.0 mL) under magnetic stirring at room temperature.

2. Add polyacrylic acid sodium salt (50 mg) as a stabilizing additive to prevent particle aggregation and control morphology. Stir until fully dissolved.

3. Introduce Ag seed nanoparticles (0.65 mg, concentration 1.0 mM) to the solution to promote heterogeneous nucleation and accelerate the reduction process.

4. Adjust the pH of the solution to approximately 10–11 using dilute NaOH solution to create alkaline conditions favorable for copper reduction.

5. Heat the solution to 60°C under continuous stirring. Slowly add N₂H₄·H₂O (hydrazine hydrate, 39.2 μL, concentration 19600 mM) dropwise as the reducing agent. The solution will gradually change color from blue to reddish-brown as Cu²⁺ ions are reduced to metallic copper.

6. Maintain the reaction at 60°C for 30–60 minutes until the reduction is complete. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature.

7. Collect the copper nanoparticles by centrifugation, wash three times with deionized water and once with ethanol to remove residual reagents, then dry under vacuum at 40°C.

Final product: Metallic copper (Cu) nanoparticles with a face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structure, spherical morphology, and particle size approximately 40 nm × 40 nm × 40 nm. Phase identification corresponds to PDF reference 04-0836.
